findings.description: The cap note is appended to the verdict reason of a *clean* second round. Trace: round 2 returns one finding {severity:"info", action:"no-op"}. `dialogue.After` sees NeedingAPerson empty and `classified.Verdict() == Clean`, so the outcome is `clean` and `end(run, Clean, verdictReason(document, classified, 2))` is called. In `verdictReason`, `len(document.Findings) != 0`, and the guard `len(classified.NeedingAPerson) == 0 && dialogue.CapReached(2)` is true, so the recorded verdict of a clean, exit-0 run reads "... The round cap of 2 was reached, so what is left is for the person rather than for another round" when nothing is left for anybody. The condition needs to be about the outcome (escalated because of the cap), not about the round number alone. No test covers this path: every second-round scenario in internal/e2e/dialogue_test.go returns either zero findings or a blocking one.

The run is published as `awaiting-response` before the round's worktree is torn down, and `scrat continue` needs that exact path. `park` saves the parked state (line 170-175) and only then does `removeWorktree` unseal (a chmod walk over the whole tree), `os.RemoveAll`, and `git worktree prune`. `scrat review --wait` returns the moment the parked state is visible (cmd/scrat/review.go:95), so the next commands a driving session issues race that teardown. `snapshot.WorktreePath` is the same path for every round, and `Checkout` runs `git worktree add --detach <path>`: while the directory is still being emptied git fails with "already exists", and in the window after RemoveAll but before prune it fails with "missing but already registered worktree". Either way `Continue` takes the `fail(...)` branch (internal/reviewer/advance.go:77) and the run ends `failed` with a git message, unrecoverably, because the responses can no longer be advanced. On a large repository the teardown is hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, so this is not a narrow window. Removing the worktree before the state is saved closes it.

A blocking finding whose action is `no-op` parks the run and then has to be answered, which is the case the requirement says the rule avoids. Trace: a round returns one finding {severity:"warning", action:"no-op"} (the prompt invites exactly this: warning is "a defect worth addressing that can honestly be taken as a follow-up", no-op is "a tradeoff worth acknowledging"). Classify puts it in NoOps, so NeedingAPerson is empty; `Classification.Verdict()` is Escalated because the severity blocks; round 1 < Cap, so the outcome is `awaiting-response`. `Responses.Unanswered` (internal/dialogue/responses.go:80) keys on severity alone, so it is reported unanswered and `scrat continue` refuses until the author fixes or rejects it. Meanwhile `scrat status` prints "findings: 1 in total, 0 for the person, 0 to patch, 1 informational" alongside "unanswered: 1", and `scrat findings` labels it "informational" (internal/report/report.go:235). So socrates demands a response to a finding it presents as asking for nothing, which is what openspec/changes/a-rejection-is-a-claim/specs/review-dialogue/spec.md:13 says parking should never do. Deciding whether the park condition is "something blocks" or "something blocks and is patchable" is a product call.

The modified requirement declares two commands that do not exist. It says the binary SHALL provide `review`, `status`, `findings`, `respond`, `continue`, `watch`, `logs` and `cancel`, and the scenario at line 14 says `scrat --help` SHALL list them. `cmd/scrat/main.go:40-48` registers no `watch` and no `logs`; those belong to the still-unstarted `one-window-three-needs` change. The change's own e2e test asserts the opposite: internal/e2e/commands_test.go:26 requires the help list to be exactly {cancel, continue, findings, help, respond, review, status}, and line 31 lists "watch" among the commands that must NOT appear. The baseline requirement this delta replaces reads "`review`, `status`, `findings` and `cancel` in this change", so the two extra commands were added here and will enter the baseline spec as satisfied when the change is archived.

`SaveResponses` is an unlocked read-modify-rewrite of the whole file, unlike the run record which is written by temp-file-plus-rename (internal/runstore/store.go:311-341). `reviewer.Respond` reads responses.json, appends one response in memory, and rewrites the file with no lock, so two `scrat respond` invocations issued concurrently (the intended consumer is an agent session, which is encouraged to run independent commands in parallel) both read the same prior state and the second write silently drops the first author's claim. A crash or a full disk mid-write leaves a truncated document, and because `Round.Responses` hard-errors on a parse failure, both `scrat respond` and `scrat continue` then exit 2 on a parked run with no way forward and the earlier claims gone. Writing through a temp file and rename, as the run record already does, removes the truncation case; serialising the read-modify-write removes the lost update.

`waitUsage` still reads "block until the review is terminal and exit with its verdict", but `--wait` now also returns on `awaiting-response` (cmd/scrat/review.go:95), which is neither terminal nor a verdict, and exits 4. The same string is the help text for `scrat continue --wait`. The run-store spec is explicit that a parked run is not a verdict, so the flag's own description is the one place that still says otherwise.

The design document for this change states the routing rule as "Nothing blocking, and nothing patchable: `clean`", which read literally sends a round with a non-blocking patchable finding to the "otherwise" case, `awaiting-response`. The implemented rule and the new requirement are "nothing blocking: clean", with a scenario ("An informational round finishes the run") that deliberately makes a non-blocking patchable round clean. The change did not touch design.md, so the design and the spec it belongs to now describe different rules for the same input.

risk_rationale:
The core routing rule, response storage and re-snapshot path are well covered by behavioural end-to-end journeys and the state machine is respected, but two reachable defects sit outside the tested paths (a wrong verdict reason on a clean second round, and a worktree teardown that races the very command it hands over to) and one park condition contradicts its own requirement.</risk_level>
